fields.problem_detail: Low soil pH (4.6) — poor early growth
fields.observations: Leaves pale and uneven on the low side of the garden. Soil test shows pH 4.6.
Mines on 10% of leaves in the lower canopy. Pheromone traps catching 15 moths a week.
Target spots on older leaves. Humidity high in the tunnel in the mornings.
Small caterpillars on outer leaves, below the threshold.
Good stand, tubers bulking well. No blight seen.
Frost on the night of 30 June burnt the outer leaves of 45% of the cabbages.
Cabbage clean. River block will be free in December.
Maize emerging well; planter set at 60 000 seeds/ha.
Leafminer pressure high again on the second tomato planting; trap counts 60 per week.

fields.advice: Apply 2 t/ha dolomitic lime on Garden 2 and work it in before the next planting.
Spray chlorantraniliprole 150 ml/ha now and again in 14 days. Keep the 3-day pre-harvest interval.
Mancozeb 2 kg/ha every 10 days while it stays humid; open the tunnel sides earlier.
Scout weekly. Spray only if more than 1 caterpillar per plant.
Harvest the undamaged heads first; sell damaged heads as Class 2 within a week.
Plant butternut on River block in December: buyers are searching for it and nobody is selling. Rotate away from cabbage.
Top-dress 150 kg/ha LAN at V6 (about 4 weeks from now).
Spray chlorantraniliprole 150 ml/ha today. Do not harvest for 7 days.

fields.title: Tomato leafminer pressure is high
fields.message: Trap counts above 50 moths a week around Polokwane. Check the lower leaves twice a week and rotate insecticide groups.

fields.title: Fall armyworm in young maize
fields.message: Moths caught near Ermelo. Scout newly emerged maize for window-pane damage on the leaves.

fields.title: Late blight weather
fields.message: Cool, wet nights forecast for the Midlands. Keep preventive copper sprays up to date.
